description: Fugue and its expander on one panel, for hosts without expander support: an eight-step sequence read by three voices, each with its own wander, step count, rest pattern and chance of sounding

params.text: Sets that step's pitch; the fader's span is one, two or five octaves depending on the menu, and hovering shows the note it quantizes to
Sets the root the sequence is quantized to, C through B
Picks the scale the sequence is quantized to, one of twelve
Sets how many of the eight steps are played before the sequence loops, 1 to 8
Sets how far each voice glides between notes; the glide time is measured against the time until that voice's next gate, so it always arrives before the note does
Sets how far that voice strays from the written pitch, from playing it exactly at one end of the travel to reaching for distant substitutions at the other
Returns all three voices to the first step on each press
Switches that voice's gate on or off for that step; with it off the voice is silent there but goes on moving through the sequence
Rolls a fresh pitch sequence for the Fugue on each press
Switches whether a voice holds its last note through a rest or a skipped step, or falls silent there
Sets how many of the eight steps that voice plays before it loops, 1 to 8, which is what lets the three voices phase against each other
Sets how far that voice's wander may reach: one, two or five octaves
Sets how many clock ticks that voice rests between active steps: 0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 16, 32, 48 or 64
Sets the chance that a step of that voice actually sounds when it is reached, none to always

inputs.text: Each rise advances that voice one step
Each rise advances that voice one step; with nothing patched it follows the clock of the voice above it
A rise returns all three voices to the first step
Moves the root, one volt per semitone, added to the root knob and wrapping round
Picks the scale, one volt per scale, added to the scale knob
Changes how many steps are played, one volt per step, added to the steps knob
Changes the glide, ±5V across the whole slew range, added to the slew knob
Changes how far that voice strays, ±5V added to its wander slider
A rise rolls a fresh pitch sequence for the Fugue
Changes how many steps that voice plays, added to its steps switch
Changes how far that voice's wander may reach, added to its range switch
Changes how many ticks that voice rests, added to its sleep switch
Changes the chance that a step of that voice sounds, added to its probability knob

outputs.text: That voice's pitch as a volt per octave, quantized to the root and scale
That voice's gate, 10V of the length set on the menu
The highest of the three voices' current pitches, whichever voice it belongs to
The middle of the three voices' current pitches, whichever voice it belongs to
The lowest of the three voices' current pitches, whichever voice it belongs to
A trigger every time that voice reaches that step

notes: only the first voice has its gates switched on to begin with; the other two are silent until their gate row is switched on
the three clock inputs are normalled downward, so one cable in the first drives all three; patching the others separately is what makes the voices polyrhythmic
the sorted outputs carry the three voices ordered by pitch rather than by name, so they give a bass part, an inner part and a top line instead of three lines that cross
menu: Fader Range — a label over the three span choices below it
1V (1 octave) — makes each pitch fader span one octave
2V (2 octaves) — makes each pitch fader span two octaves
5V (5 octaves) — makes each pitch fader span five octaves
Harmonic Lock — makes each voice weigh what the other two are playing before it strays, picking the most consonant of three candidates; turning it off lets each voice stray on its own
Gate length: Clock passthrough, Trigger (1ms), 25%, 50%, 75%, 90%, 100% (legato) — sets how much of each step the gate outputs hold high
Trigger width — sets how long the gate lasts when its length is set to Trigger: a fixed 1, 2, 5 or 10ms
Randomize Sequence — rolls a fresh pitch sequence, which is what the panel button does by hand
